recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. FHIR-I should decide whether the FHIR Extension Pack needs a new time-only or Timing-specific extension for prescribed time windows, and only add core narrative guidance later if the work group explicitly wants a core reference to that external extension.
issue_request: FHIR-39336 asked FHIR-core to let Timing express that a recurring action should occur between one time-of-day and another; Jira status is Published with Persuasive resolution stating it was dealt with as part of FHIR-38726's new uncertainty extensions.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-39336. The related FHIR-38726 commit 5436c013544f8333aabd7d6f919afb9987922887 added uncertainPeriod to the active element-extensions spreadsheet, but that row applied only to date and dateTime and used valuePeriod. Commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 then removed those extension definitions from R5 core source.
additional_context: Current core source/fhir.ini still includes the element-extension spreadsheet, but current core datatype and element-extension sources contain no uncertainPeriod, uncertainTime, or timing-uncertainDate definition rows. The surviving definitions are in the FHIR Extension Pack: uncertainPeriod is scoped to date and dateTime and timing-uncertainDate is deprecated/retired in favor of uncertainPeriod by FHIR-41649. FHIR-I minutes on 2023-02-13 record the related FHIR-38726/FHIR-39336 distinction between descriptive and prescriptive uncertainty, including a 2-4 pm example, and say the work would be pulled out of R5 for later discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty human-review audit commit on the combined branch. No core source change was made because adding a time-only bound extension would now belong in the Extension Pack and would require resolving the work-group semantic question rather than making a safe surgical FHIR-core edit.
